definition: A model specifically trained to convert text (or other data) into dense vector representations optimized for tasks like similarity search or clustering.
details: Embedding models are a distinct category from generative LLMs, optimized for producing representations useful for downstream retrieval and comparison tasks rather than for generating fluent text.
story: Picture an architect laying out a building where every room has to know which other rooms matter to it. In plain words: A model specifically trained to convert text (or other data) into dense vector representations optimized for tasks like similarity search or clustering. Here is how it actually plays out: Embedding models are a distinct category from generative LLMs, optimized for producing representations useful for downstream retrieval and comparison tasks rather than for generating fluent text. It is the difference between a row of isolated cubicles and one big room where everyone can hear each other. That blueprint is Embedding Model.
